conclusion.classification: High-confidence test observation/completion-contract race; not evidence yet of a persistent production lease leak
conclusion.mechanism: TaskService.kill returns void and starts managed stop without awaiting it. Synthetic CLI/bridge exit callbacks also update the SQLite lifecycle asynchronously. ApplicationService.dispose owns business contexts/upstream pools but does not join ManagedTaskCapabilities run/bridge/hold shutdown. The test asserts all capability leases released before awaiting that separate owner.
conclusion.confidenceBoundary: CI reports only the count, not lease owner_kind/owner_id/run state. Read-only analysis cannot prove exactly which lease was still pending or prove the eventual post-drain count. A completion-aligned targeted verification remains required.
conclusion.whyDifferentRunsCanDiffer: Unrelated ApplicationService/upstream disposal may happen to take long enough for managed shutdown on one run, but it is not its synchronization contract.

recommendation.changeType: Test/fixture completion boundary only; no production change justified by this count alone
recommendation.preferredShutdown: Keep project A/B isolation assertions unchanged. At final shutdown, kill remaining B, assert drainFixtureBridgeExits returns no failures, await managed.dispose, then await applications.dispose, mirroring the real host owner order; retain pool empty, actual child PID exited and global lease zero assertions.

recommendation.ifStillFailing: Capture remaining active lease rows including owner_kind/owner_id/resource_id, joined capability_runs state/revocation/task_id, process rows and active activities. A nonzero lease after the managed completion barrier is materially different and must be treated as a potential product defect.
